 Nayeem refuses to give up hope despite Bangladesh's batting collapse
 It was a dramatic day in Mirpur, with 12 wickets falling. Bangladesh began the day by bowling out the West Indies and taking a 27-run first-innings lead. However, their batting fell apart in the second innings.
 Written by : Khan Mutasim Billah Life 
 Posted - Oct 30, 2026, 11:18 pm 2026-10-30T23:18:33+06:00 
 Updated - Oct 30, 2026, 11:18 pm 2026-10-30T23:18:33+06:00 
 Bangladesh find themselves in a difficult position after the third day of the Mirpur Test. Despite holding a 106-run lead, the Tigers have only four wickets remaining. Even though the pitch is offering plenty of turn, Bangladesh will need a much bigger total to put themselves in a strong position to win the match.
 It was a dramatic day in Mirpur, with 12 wickets falling. Bangladesh began the day by bowling out the West Indies and taking a 27-run first-innings lead. However, their batting fell apart in the second innings.
 The Tigers finished the day on 79 for 6, taking their overall lead to 106 runs. Jaker Ali Anik and Nayeem Hasan were unbeaten at the crease when play ended.
 Get Latest Cricket Updates on WhatsApp Despite the difficult situation, Bangladesh spinner Nayeem Hasan has not lost hope. Speaking at the post-day press conference as Bangladesh's representative, he said the team still believes it can win. "Insha’Allah, if we can set a good target, anything is possible with Allah's will. We'll try to score as many runs as we can. The more runs we get, the better. I believe Zakir bhai and I can build a big partnership," Nayeem said.
 He also believes the West Indies ' attacking approach could create opportunities for Bangladesh. "Cricket is a game of runs. If they attack, we'll get opportunities. If we can make the most of those chances, it will be good for us. A good target will put us in a better position. Even after losing so many wickets, everyone remained calm because we believe someone can take responsibility and carry the team," he added.
 Nayeem is still at the crease and hopes to make a valuable contribution with the bat. He said he sees himself as a batter when he has the bat in his hands and tries to do whatever the team needs. "When I have the ball in my hand, I'm a bowler. When I have the bat, I'm a batter. Everyone has to bat, and I try to do whatever the team needs from me. Insha’Allah, Jaker bhai and I will try to bat for as long as possible. The more we score, the better it will be for us. If we can reach 200, that would be really good," he said.
 Talking about his batting approach, Nayeem said there was no special plan. He simply tried to respond to the deliveries as they came. "There wasn't any particular plan. I just tried to play the shots according to the deliveries. Scoring runs isn't easy on this pitch because the ball is turning. But if we keep the scoreboard moving, the bowlers will come under pressure," he explained.
 Nayeem also defended his teammates after Bangladesh's batting collapse, saying no batter can perform well every day. He believes the team still has a chance to fight back. "Everyone doesn't play well every day. Now the opportunity is in our hands. If we can make the most of it, we can come back from this position. Big teams often fight back from difficult situations, and Insha’Allah, Jaker bhai and I will try to do the same," he said.
 Follow google news channel to get news of BDCricTime. He also pointed out that batting had not been easy throughout the day, particularly under the lights when the ball was behaving differently. "Shadman Islam bhai and the others batted under the lights at the start. The ball was doing different things. Sometimes it was coming straight, and sometimes it was turning. We should have batted a little better, but that's part of the game. Insha’Allah, we'll try to come back from here," Nayeem added.
